title: Tenant fence probing, reservation rightsizing, and burst governor roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up ticket for the recent dedicated-cluster capacity event where multiple tenants caused sustained tail-latency degradation. This work bundles a short-term tenant isolation probe, a rightsizing audit for reservation allocations, and a rework of the burst governor behavior to reduce eviction storms. Goal: reduce P99 latency regressions and prevent cross-tenant spillover during sudden traffic surges.
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha P: Triage concluded — incident traced to overlapping soft-reservations + aggressive burst credits. Immediate mitigation: increase eviction threshold, apply temporary tenant fencing for top 3 noisy tenants.

2025-02-14 Marco C: Telemetry summary attached. KV cache pressure correlated with tenant X and heavy beam-search workloads. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood-inference/internal/dedicated/capacity-2025-02-12

2025-02-15 Elena R (SRE): Ran a fault-injection probe to validate tenant-fence logic; probe showed that soft-fence prevented eviction cascade but introduced higher 95th latency for fenced tenants. Logged results in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood-inference/display/CAP/tenant-fence-probes

2025-02-16 Marco C: Proposal v1 posted — (1) build 'probe mode' for tenant fencing (non-destructive, metrics-only), (2) run reservation rightsizing sweep using 7-day tail percentiles, (3) replace linear burst decay with exponential governor to smooth token buckets. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/1823
2025-02-18 PM review (Jonas K): Support for probe mode is approved; ensure UI shows probe vs enforced state to avoid confusion for operations. Add telemetry for burst reuse rates.

2025-02-20 Design feedback (Maya L): Console should surface tenant fencing state in the dedicated cluster view and include a recommended action (e.g., 'recommend reservation + burst limit') with one-click apply to test tenants.

2025-02-22 SRE note (Elena R): Synthetic re-run after provisional rightsizing shows 27% fewer eviction events and 12% P99 improvement on test clusters. Results: https://dashboards.redwood-inference/internal/experiments/rightsize-2025-02-22

2025-02-24 Marco C: Implemented burst governor prototype; unit tests added and integration tests scheduled. Performance bench on a c6x-large GPU node shows stable throughput with reduced transient oversubscription.
2025-02-25 Security review (Priya S): No secrets/external data flows introduced. KMS path unchanged. Marking security_review_required=false.
acceptance_criteria: Probe mode: telemetry-only tenant fencing can be enabled cluster-wide without dropping requests and emits clear metrics to ops dashboard
Rightsizing sweep: automated job produces per-tenant recommended reservation adjustments with delta <25% for low-variance tenants and flagged high-variance tenants for manual review
Burst governor: new exponential decay implementation reduces eviction cascade frequency by >=20% in synthetic spike tests
Console: dedicated cluster view surfaces probe vs enforce state with explicit action buttons and audit log entries
Rollout plan: canary on 5% of clusters, automated rollback if eviction rate increases vs baseline

Schedule canary rollout for probe-only tenant fencing to two non-production clusters (assigned: SRE, due: 2025-03-02)
Run reservation rightsizing sweep on staging and compare recommended deltas to historical billing/latency data (assigned: Data Eng, due: 2025-02-27)
